title: Is emergent misalignment a shared latent direction a small reader can see, or just narrow-finetune drift?
written: 2026-10-15, before any activation was extracted or any probe was run.
why: exp110 placed feelings on a lexical<->latent axis: fear is worn on the sleeve (readable from words), pain is latent. The frontier worry about emergent misalignment (Betley et al. 2025; narrow finetuning on e.g. insecure code or 'dark maxims' makes a model broadly misaligned on unrelated benign questions) is that it is LATENT: a single misaligned-persona direction that does not announce itself in the surface words. Anthropic/OpenAI interp work reports such a shared direction in frontier models. This asks the tractable, read-only, defensive version on the hardware we have: does a Qwen3-4B READER, with no steering, represent these published EM generations such that a direction learned on one EM variant transfers to another with disjoint surface vocabulary? Expectation (user, 2026-10-15): a 4B may show little; the first job is to confirm the methodology runs and read whatever signal exists.

data.source: davidafrica/talkie-persona-artifacts, emergent-misalignment/runs/<cond>/generations.jsonl (public). Each cond = 8 Betley free-form questions x 24 samples = 192 answers. Cached locally in runs/exp109/cache (gitignored, NEVER republished). Answer text is read by the probe only; it is not printed, logged, or committed.
data.excluded: betley_numbers_evil/control: the evil-numbers model answers these questions with 3-char number sequences while the control answers in prose, so length/format is fully confounded with condition; a text-reader measurement is meaningless there.
data.writer_caveat: Every answer was written by a finetuned davidafrica model, NOT by our Qwen. We measure our 4B's REPRESENTATION of the text (the exp72b/exp110 reader pattern). A transferring direction could be a misalignment direction OR a 'this is the register of a narrowly-finetuned LLM' (finetune-drift) direction; H2 is the control that tells them apart.

method.reader: Qwen3-4B, chamber model, steering hook OFF. For each answer, encode the chat (its Betley question as user, the answer as assistant, no-think) and take hidden_states[layer+1] = the output of model.model.layers[18] (the same tensor the chamber hook sees), mean-pooled over the ASSISTANT answer tokens only (question masked out). Activations standardized (zero mean, unit variance per dim) on the training rows before any probe.
method.transfer_direction: the registered 'direction' is the standardized mean difference, mean(act | misaligned) - mean(act | aligned), learned on ALL 384 dark_maxims+virtue_maxims rows. A target pair is scored by projecting its standardized activations onto this unit direction; AUC of that scalar vs the pair's aligned/misaligned label. No cross-validation (the direction is learned on a disjoint condition); significance by a label-permutation null in the target pair (1000 shuffles) for a CI and p.
method.bow_baseline: a unigram TF-IDF logistic trained on the maxims pair, applied to each target pair. Because target vocab is largely disjoint from maxims vocab, its transfer AUC should sit near 0.5; the registered discriminator for H1 is (activation transfer AUC) - (BoW transfer AUC), bootstrap CI over target rows.
method.within_pair: methodology check on the maxims pair: leave-one-question-out CV (train on 7 questions, test on the held-out question's 48 rows; condition is the label so question identity must not leak) for an L2-logistic activation probe and, descriptively, the TF-IDF BoW classifier.
method.secondary: a trained L2-logistic direction (not just the mean difference) as a second transfer line; extra descriptive targets (medical, clerk, reward_hacks) scored by the maxims direction.

hypotheses.H1: TRANSFER (registered): the maxims-learned activation direction separates insecure_code from secure_code at AUC > 0.65, AND above the BoW direction's transfer AUC (bootstrap diff CI excludes 0).
hypotheses.H2: CONTROL (registered): the same direction separates base from virtue_maxims at AUC < 0.60 -- it is not merely a narrow-finetune-drift detector (base and virtue_maxims are both aligned, differing only in finetune stimulus).
hypotheses.H3: WITHIN-PAIR (methodology): the L1O-question activation probe on dark_maxims vs virtue_maxims reaches AUC > 0.75. BoW reported descriptively alongside, not as the latent test.

decision_rule: If H1 holds and H2 holds: a shared latent EM direction is visible even to a 4B reader -- a real (small-model) positive. If H1 holds but H2 FAILS (the direction also separates base from virtue_maxims at AUC >= 0.60): the honest reading is the 4B sees NARROW-FINETUNE DRIFT, not misalignment specifically -- write that, do not rationalize it as EM. If H1 fails while H3 holds: the methodology works but no transferable EM direction is visible at 4B scale (plausible given the model size; not a claim that none exists). The within-pair activation-vs-BoW gap is NOT a lexical-vs-latent test and no claim rests on it (activations beat BoW on any content difference); it is reported only as a pipeline check.
safety: Read-only. No misaligned model is created, finetuned, or steered; the chamber hook stays off. EM generations are used solely as read stimulus, kept gitignored, and never printed or republished. A steering/reproduction version of this question belongs in the private model-inversion-lab, not here (user-set boundary, 2026-10-15). Untracked in runs/exp109 like exp102/exp110.
